ruling.recommended_action: Reject the rider's $6.15 refund request; no further action. Optionally confirm with the rider that the 12:01:40 in-app notice (new 1.4× multiplier, revised $29.75 estimate, free cancellation) satisfied SURGE-1.
ruling.reasoning:
No safety issue: the chat is a pickup arrangement (F10–F12) and the driver's statement (F13) contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — safety screen clean.

Fare dispute turns on SURGE-1/SURGE-2. The quote of $21.67 was at 1× (F6); the surge rose to 1.4× at trip start (F4, F7). SURGE-1 requires an in-app notice before or at pickup stating (a) the new multiplier, (b) the revised estimated fare, and (c) free cancellation. The surge log (F9) shows an in-app notice at 12:01:40, i.e. before the trip started at 12:02:00, stating "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" (new multiplier), "Your new estimated fare is $29.75" (revised fare) and "You can cancel for free" (free cancellation). All three items are present and the notice preceded trip start, so the rider was notified under SURGE-1.

Because the rider was notified and rode, SURGE-2 row 1 applies: no_action. The rider's claim that the notice came too late is contradicted by the timestamped system log [system records override statements].

The surge differential is (1.4 − 1) × $18.82 = $7.53 (F8); were notice missing, a partial refund would be capped at the $6.15 the fare exceeded the quote (SURGE-3). That refund is not owed on these facts. Route is not in issue: actual 8.6 km vs optimal 8.7 km is a −0.1 km deviation, within RD-1 tolerance (F1–F3).

Amount: none. $6.15 refund denied. Driver's 2 upheld disputes (F15) are both non-route, non-no-show and do not trigger RD-6 or NS-9; the profile does not decide the case. Amount involved is $6.15, under $10, so a system ruling is final (TH-1/TH-2); confidence is high on complete records (GPS, fares, timestamped notice).
